name: Payroll tax
what: Register and pay payroll tax in each state where wages exceed that state's threshold.
consistency_note: Most states harmonised parts of payroll tax administration, but each sets its own rate, threshold and exemptions.

basis.source: NSW Productivity Commission White Paper 2021: Rebooting the economy
basis.quote: Jurisdictional differences in payroll tax administration can distort competition between states, by encouraging business to set-up in states with lower compliance costs.

issues.what: Each state sets its own payroll tax thresholds, rates, exemptions and administration, so an employer in several states files and calculates under several regimes.

evidence.source: Australia's Future Tax System: Report to the Treasurer, Part Two, Volume 2 (Henry review)
evidence.quote: While there are similarities in the main taxes used in each State, the thresholds, rates and range of exemptions often differ between States.

evidence.source: NSW Productivity Commission White Paper 2021: Rebooting the economy
evidence.quote: Employers operating in more than one state and territory would benefit from a common set of rules for payroll tax administration. Their tax would be simpler and their compliance costs would fall.

issues.status_note: NSW committed to implement its 2018 review of payroll tax administration; the NSW Productivity Commission (2021) proposed a national coordination body for consistent administration.

issues.what: Thresholds and exemptions make payroll tax more complex than it needs to be.

evidence.source: Australia's Future Tax System: Report to the Treasurer, Part Two, Volume 1 (Henry review)
evidence.quote: Existing payroll taxes are more complex and less efficient than they could be because of tax-free thresholds and other exemptions.
